question: Which of the following sessions of the Indian National Congress was headed by Sarojini Naidu?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kanpur, 1925**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kanpur Session of 1925** was presided over by **Sarojini Naidu**, making her the first Indian woman to head the Indian National Congress.
 
• Her election as the president marked a significant milestone in the history of the Indian freedom struggle, showcasing the role of women leaders.
 
• During her tenure as the Congress president, Sarojini Naidu emphasized the importance of communal harmony and national unity.
 
• The session contributed to promoting the Gandhian ideals of Swaraj and non-violence as central tenets of the freedom movement.
 
• Sarojini Naidu was also known as the "Nightingale of India" for her contributions to Indian poetry and her eloquence in addressing public gatherings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress:**

 
 
• Founded in **1885**, the Indian National Congress was pivotal in the Indian independence movement.
 
• It was initially established to create a platform for civil and political dialogue among educated Indians.
 
 
 
• **Role of Women in the Freedom Struggle:**
 
 
• Women leaders like Sarojini Naidu, Annie Besant, and Kamala Nehru played key roles in shaping India's independence movement.
 
• They contributed through speeches, protests, and active participation in leadership roles.
 
 
 
• **Gandhian Philosophy:**
 
 
• Mahatma Gandhi advocated for Swaraj (self-rule), non-violence, and communal harmony as the pillars of the freedom struggle.
 
• These ideals were deeply ingrained in Congress sessions and activities during the independence movement.
 
 
 
• **Sarojini Naidu's Legacy:**
 
 
• She served as the Governor of Uttar Pradesh post-independence, becoming the first woman to hold a governorship in independent India.
 
• Her poetry, speeches, and activism continue to inspire generations in India and globally.
